title: Pasta (Spaghetti) Carbonara
description:
If you ever want a late night or après ski supper that’s really easy and really good, this is it. You probably have most of the key ingredients laying around – pasta, cheese, garlic, eggs, maybe bacon or some other salty bit of meat – but if not, improvise a little.
If you don’t have eggs and bacon, you can make “Spaghetti Hallelujah,” (really Spaghetti alla Olio, a traditional meatless pasta dish, for old-fashioned Christmas Eve).
Of course, if you don’t have pasta, you’re stuck. If you only have eggs, we suggest that you make an omelet.
Anyway, back to the Carbonara. The real Italian version is made with Italian bacon – pancetta – or maybe prosciutto, but here we usually use bacon because it’s often around and it tastes so good in this combination.
Of course, a nice glass of hearty red wine is good here too.
Mange e bevi!
ingredients: 1 pound spaghetti more Parmesan/Romano for serving (If making half this recipe, I recommend using 2 eggs and 2 garlic cloves.)
directions: When water comes to a boil, add the pasta, stir to separate, and cook until al dente.

Meanwhile, add the wine and all but a big pinch of the minced garlic to the bacon pan and simmer until the alcohol aroma has cooked off and the wine is slightly reduced, 6 to 8 minutes. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
Beat eggs, cheeses, and remaining pinch of garlic together with a fork in a small bowl; set aside.
When the pasta is done, reserve 1+ cups of the pasta cooking water and drain it, leaving the pasta slightly wet. Transfer the drained pasta to the warmed serving bowl.
If pasta is dry or sticky, add some reserved cooking water and toss to moisten. (This is important for the egg sauce to mix in well.)
Slowly whisk ½ cup or so of the drained pasta water into the egg mixture and pour it all over the hot pasta and toss well.
Pour the bacon mixture over the pasta, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and toss well to combine. Serve immediately with extra Parmesan/Romano for the table.
Set a large heatproof serving bowl on rack, and heat oven to 200 degrees.
Bring a big pot of salted water to boil.
While water is heating, cut the bacon into little bits by first slicing lengthwise down the middle, then cutting crosswise.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium heat until shimmering, but not smoking. Add the bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and crisp, about 8 minutes.
